author: Rick Fritz
text: I’ve been the Pharma/med device supply chain industry for decades and the manufacturer is required to ensure products remain within the labeled temp range during transit up to the pharmacy.  Once it gets to the pharmacy, they are then responsible for the product, not when delivered to your house.  Ask Abbott if they allow for temp excursions before the product degrades.

author: Gene Holcombe
text:
I agree with your thesis.  That’s why you should buy from pharmacies or trusted DME suppliers.  They have storage facilities designed for keeping sensors at the required temp.  Now once you order sensors and they are being shipped they have no more control. If ups, usps or other delivery services keep them in hot conditions or in a hot mailbox it could affect the sensor.  Best option is to buy from pharmacies and take home directly.  Secondly, get your sensors inside as soon as delivered.  
It might be interesting to do a poll to ask how people get their sensors and how transported
